title: Relative coslice restriction is a left fibration
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns, quasicategories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner and left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. For simplicial sets $A,T$, define the ordered join by
$$(A\star T)_r=A_r\amalg T_r\amalg\coprod_{u,v\geq0,\ u+v+1=r} A_u\times T_v,$$
with operators restricting the ordered concatenation of the $A$-vertices followed by the $T$-vertices. Let $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories, let $K_0\hookrightarrow K$ be a monomorphism of small simplicial sets, and let $f:K\to\mathcal C$ with $f_0=f|_{K_0}$. Define the coherent join coslice $(\mathcal C_{f/})_r$ to be the maps $K\star\Delta^r\to\mathcal C$ restricting to $f$ on $K$, with operators induced by $\operatorname{id}_K\star\Delta(\alpha)$; define the analogous coslices for $f_0$, $qf$ and $qf_0$. Their projections restrict a simplex to its last block $\Delta^r$; restriction from $K$ to $K_0$ and postcomposition with $q$ define maps between the coslices. Put
$$\mathcal E=\mathcal C_{f_0/}\times_{\mathcal D_{qf_0/}}\mathcal D_{qf/}.$$
Then all four coslices and $\mathcal E$ are quasicategories. The map
$$\rho:\mathcal C_{f/}\longrightarrow\mathcal E,\qquad h\longmapsto(h|_{K_0\star\Delta^r},q h),$$
and the map
$$\theta:\mathcal E\longrightarrow\mathcal C,\qquad (h_0,k)\longmapsto h_0|_{\Delta^r},$$
are left fibrations: they lift every $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i<m$.

proof.text: For any nonempty small simplicial set $T$, a simplicial map $T\to\mathcal C_{f/}$ is equivalent to a map $K\star T\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction to $K$ is $f$. Indeed, restrict to $K\star\Delta^r$ for each simplex $\Delta^r\to T$. Conversely, on a mixed simplex $(x,t)\in K_u\times T_v$ use the map associated to $t:\Delta^v\to T$ on the corresponding mixed simplex of $K\star\Delta^v$; on the pure summands use $f$ and the last-block restrictions. For an operator restricting a mixed simplex to two nonempty blocks, restrict its first block in $K$ and its second block in $T$; naturality of the family associated to the second-block simplex gives exactly the same value as first evaluating and then restricting. If the second block disappears, the value is the corresponding restriction of $f$; if the first block disappears, it is the last-block restriction of the same family member. This also checks degeneracies, where a block is repeated rather than deleted. Evaluating the reconstructed map on $K\star\Delta^r$ recovers each original family member on both pure summands and on every mixed summand, and reconstruction from a join map recovers each of its summand values. Thus the constructions are inverse. Nonemptiness ensures that the pure $K$-summand is tested; all horns used below are nonempty, including $\Lambda_0^1=\{0\}$. The same description applies to each of the other three coslices. All maps and pullbacks in the statement are therefore actual simplicial maps and degreewise small simplicial sets.

source.place: Unwinding join coslices before the relative lifting square; explicit degreewise argument.

proof.text: Use the definition of inner anodyne in [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation]. Every inner fibration $q:X\to S$ lifts against every inner anodyne map, with the prescribed map to $S$ retained. The generating inner horns lift by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. For a pushout, restrict the square to the attached map, choose its lift, and glue it to the given map. For a continuous ordinal composite, extend over each successor over the fixed bottom map and at each limit glue the compatible maps degreewise. Isomorphisms lift using their inverse. For an arrow retract $i:A\to B$ of $j:A'\to B'$ with section $(s_A,s_B)$ and retraction $(r_A,r_B)$, a square $(u:A\to X,v:B\to S)$ for $i$ gives the square $(ur_A,vr_B)$ for $j$. If $h':B'\to X$ lifts it, $h's_B$ extends $u$ because $h's_Bi=h'js_A=ur_As_A=u$, and $qh's_B=vr_Bs_B=v$. Thus the lifting class contains the weakly saturated class generated by the inner horns.

source.place: Inner-anodyne lifting used at the end of the proof; the saturation closure argument is supplied explicitly.

proof.text:
Fix $k:\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i<m$. For $a:\partial\Delta^p\hookrightarrow\Delta^p$, $p\geq0$, the pushout-join $\theta_{a,k}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation] identifies with
$$\Lambda_{p+1+i}^{p+m+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{p+m+1}.$$
Order the $p+1$ first-factor vertices before the $m+1$ second-factor vertices. The piece $\partial\Delta^p\star\Delta^m$ supplies the faces omitting first-factor vertices; the piece $\Delta^p\star\Lambda_i^m$ supplies the faces omitting second-factor vertices other than the vertex numbered $p+1+i$. A simplex belongs to these unions exactly when its image omits one of those vertices, so the equality holds in every degree. The omitted index is inner since $0<p+1+i<p+m+1$. This includes $p=0$, when $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, and $m=1,i=0$, when the omitted index is $p+1$. Hence each boundary inclusion belongs to the weakly saturated class of monomorphisms $a$ for which $\theta_{a,k}$ is inner anodyne, supplied by the cited saturation lemma. A simplicial monomorphism is degreewise injective: an $r$-simplex $x$ determines the map $\Delta^r\to A$ sending $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$ to $A(\alpha)(x)$; equality of the images of two $r$-simplices makes these maps equal after composition to $B$, so monomorphism cancellation and evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_{[r]}$ make the simplices equal. Identify $A$ with its simplicial image in $B$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to this degreewise injection: its stages are pushouts of coproducts of boundary inclusions. Well-order each set of cells and attach them successively, so a coproduct attachment is a transfinite composite of pushouts of individual boundary inclusions. At limit stages take the degreewise union; then take the union of the dimension stages. Weak saturation gives
$$(A\star\Delta^m)\cup_{A\star\Lambda_i^m}(B\star\Lambda_i^m)\hookrightarrow B\star\Delta^m$$
inner anodyne for every monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, generating-horn calculation with the left horn in the second variable; 0077 supplies the boundary-cell reduction.

proof.text:
Consider any left-horn square for $\rho$, with top $a:\Lambda_i^m\to\mathcal C_{f/}$ and bottom $(h_0,k):\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$. By step 1 these are maps on joins. The equality $\rho a=(h_0,k)|_{\Lambda_i^m}$ says both that the top map and $h_0$ agree on $K_0\star\Lambda_i^m$, and that its composite with $q$ is $k$ on $K\star\Lambda_i^m$. Membership of $(h_0,k)$ in the fiber product says $qh_0=k|_{K_0\star\Delta^m}$. They therefore define a commutative square against $q$ with left map
$$(K_0\star\Delta^m)\cup_{K_0\star\Lambda_i^m}(K\star\Lambda_i^m)\hookrightarrow K\star\Delta^m,$$
upper map given by $h_0$ and $a$, and lower map $k$. The left map is inner anodyne by step 3, so step 2 gives a lift $h$ over exactly $k$. The pure $K$-summand is already in the upper domain and has map $f$, so $h$ defines a simplex of $\mathcal C_{f/}$. Its restriction is exactly $a$, and $\rho h=(h_0,k)$. This proves every required horn lift for $\rho$. The argument used only that $q$ is an inner fibration, not that its source and target are quasicategories.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8, coslice half: translate the relative square and lift over its specified base simplex.

proof.text: For any small quasicategory $Q$ and $g:K\to Q$, apply the general argument of step 4 to $Q\to\Delta^0$. This map is an inner fibration because every inner horn in $Q$ fills; all coslices of $\Delta^0$ are the one-point simplicial set. Thus $Q_{g/}\to Q_{g_0/}$ is a left fibration for every $K_0\hookrightarrow K$. With $K_0=\varnothing$ the target is $Q$, since $\varnothing\star\Delta^r=\Delta^r$, and the map is exactly the last-block projection. Each $Q_{g/}$ is a quasicategory: project an inner horn to $Q$, choose a filler there, then lift that fixed simplex along this projection. Applying this to $Q=\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and $g=f,f_0,qf,qf_0$ proves the four coslice assertions and proves that both the projection $\mathcal C_{f_0/}\to\mathcal C$ and the restriction $\mathcal D_{qf/}\to\mathcal D_{qf_0/}$ are left fibrations.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.6.12, terminal-base specialization of 01BZ; 018F is its empty-subset case.

proof.text: Factor $\theta$ as the first-coordinate projection $\pi:\mathcal E\to\mathcal C_{f_0/}$ followed by the last-block projection $s:\mathcal C_{f_0/}\to\mathcal C$. The first is the degreewise pullback of the left fibration $\mathcal D_{qf/}\to\mathcal D_{qf_0/}$ established in step 5. Explicitly, a left-horn square for $\pi$ prescribes a simplex $h_0$ in $\mathcal C_{f_0/}$; composing it with $q$ gives the bottom simplex for that restriction map. Lift its given $k$-coordinate and pair the lift with $h_0$. This is a lift for $\pi$. To solve a left-horn square for $s\pi$, first use the lifting property of $s$ to extend its $\mathcal C_{f_0/}$-coordinate over the prescribed simplex in $\mathcal C$, and then use the just-proved property of $\pi$. Their composite lift solves the original square, so $\theta$ is a left fibration. Finally an inner horn in $\mathcal E$ projects along $\theta$ to one in the quasicategory $\mathcal C$; fill there and lift that particular filler. Thus $\mathcal E$ is a quasicategory. These are exactly the displayed maps in the statement, with no change of base simplex and no extra condition on $K_0\hookrightarrow K$.
